text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on July 22 in history:
1456 - Hungarian general Janos Hunyadi defeated the Turks besieging Belgrade.
1478 - Philip I "The Handsome", King of Castile and founder of the Habsburg dynasty in Spain, born; son of Emperor Maximilian.
1515 - The Congress of Vienna settled points at issue between Poland and the Holy Roman Empire and the succession to the Hungarian throne.
1691 - The Anglo-Dutch army defeated the French at Aghrim, India.
1739 - The Turks defeated troops of the Holy Roman Empire at Crocyka, Yugoslavia, and threatened Belgrade.
1784 - Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel, German astronomer and mathematician who calculated the path of Halley's Comet, born.
1812 - The Duke of Wellington defeated the French under Marshal Marmont at the battle of Salamanca.
1883 - Lev Borisovich Kamenev, Russian revolutionary and politician, born. He was shot in 1936 for conspiring against Stalin, but was posthumously found not guilty of the crime.
1888 - Selman Abraham Waksman, U.S. microbiologist, born in what is now Ukraine; he won the Nobel Prize for Medicine in 1952 for his discovery of streptomycin.
1890 - Rose Kennedy, mother of John F. Robert and Edward Kennedy, born.
1892 - Arthur Seyss-Inquart, Austrian Nazi chief during its annexation by Germany 1938-39, born. He was executed for war crimes in 1946.
1898 - Stephen Vincent Benet, U.S. short story writer and poet, born; best known for his poem on the U.S. Civil War, "John Brown's Body".
1899 - King Sobhuza II of Swaziland born; he reigned for over 60 years from 1921 until his death in 1982.
1913 - Licia Albanese, Italian-born soprano, born; best remembered for her roles at New York's Metropolitan Opera and for her recording of La Boheme conducted by Arturo Toscanini.
1917 - Alexander Kerensky became prime minister of Russia, taking over from Prince Lvov.
1932 - Florenz Ziegfeld, U.S. theatrical producer and impresario, died; famed for his "Follies" spectacular revues which ran every year from 1907-31.
1933 - Wiley Post, U.S. pioneer aviator, became the first person to fly solo around the world, in seven days 18 hours 49 minutes.
1934 - U.S. bank robber and public enemy number one John Dillinger was shot dead by FBI agents outside Chicago's Biograph Theatre after 13 months on the run.
1943 - U.S. forces liberated Palermo, Sicily.
1950 - William Lyon Mackenzie King, Canadian Liberal statesman and three times prime minister, died.
1950 - King Leopold III returned to Belgium after six years in exile.
1972 - The European Economic Community (EEC) and European Free Trade Area (EFTA) agreed on a new free trade area linking the two organisations, effective January 1, 1973.
1974 - Two days after invading Cyprus, Turkey accepted a U.N. resolution on a ceasefire.
1981 - Mehmet Ali Agca was jailed for life for the attempted murder of Pope John Paul II.
1993 - Japanese Prime Minister Kiichi Miyazawa resigned as president of the Liberal Democratic Party, taking the blame for party's worst-ever election performance.
1995 - Harold Larwood, English fast bowler, died. He spearheaded the attack on Australia's batsmen in the notorious "bodyline" cricket series of the early 1930s.
